Replay

Browser UI acceptance

1 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓

The UI test runs three independent Chrome processes against the actual exported Scrapyard game and local authenticated WebRTC room fixture. It drives real canvas keyboard/mouse input for chat, middle-mouse pings, shop cards, ability keys and revival. A query-parameter-gated test node supplies observations and prepares funds/wounds/jams through the existing admitted development actions. Ordnance checks use the existing manual firing-control driver and bounded scene samples.

Shell
RSB_UI_LOGS=/absolute/output/directory \
  nix develop --command bash examples/replay_scrapyard/web_ui_run.sh

The test checks muster previews, both picker directions, readiness clearing, host Start, and late Drop In through the actual buttons.

UI checks cover chat focus/cancellation and plain text, late-join history without expired markers, ping delivery/expiry, purchase accounting without gunfire, plate/jam/cooldown HUD state, teammate camera/revival, Escape menu input/focus/resizing, and tally release while chatting.

Combat presentation checks cover rail contact sparks, grenade bounce/embers/fuse expiry, slime/sparkjar/spit discs on owner and remote screens, filled nova fades, single buff bursts, constant zone fill/expiry, the local/remote cone distinction, and recorded spread bolts. The test also compares whole-world hashes, reaches the natural barrel wipe and next-yard recovery, and quits one peer through the menu. The remaining yard must continue and remove that player's row. It uses an empty single wave to reach the shop, later adds one spitter for the disc check, and disables audio. It does not replace the separate combat, migration, storage or hardware-listening gates.

REPLAY_PREBUILT=1 reuses current native/WASM artifacts but still runs the Godot release export. Run it inside the Nix shell: the export plugin needs the compiler toolchain even when the script's explicit build stage is skipped.

Recorded results include inspected captures and a build-time fix. A full-frame fallback assignment in the chat-history adapter produced costly aggregate lowering; using a separate owned read removed the aggregate store and restored a short standard web build. No optimizer passes or gameplay validation were disabled.

Additional browsers/devices, named-observer metadata, broader presentation, hardware listening, human playtests and full comparison remain requirements.
